findings.source_passage: Quoin is not a Euclidean term. It belongs to the pure nautical mathematics. I know not that it has been defined before. A quoin is a solid which differs from a wedge in having its sharp end formed by the steep inclination of one side, instead of the mutual tapering of both sides.
findings.why_it_matters: The full footnote definition — 'A quoin is a solid which differs from a wedge in having its sharp end formed by the steep inclination of one side, instead of the mutual tapering of both sides' — is Melville's characteristic pseudo-scholarly pedantry; it is voice-establishing and interpretively distinctive, yet the draft drops the actual definition entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the complete footnote definition verbatim: 'A quoin is a solid which differs from a wedge in having its sharp end formed by the steep inclination of one side, instead of the mutual tapering of both sides.'

findings.source_passage: the Case, may be regarded as the great Heidelburgh Tun of the Sperm Whale. And as that famous great tierce is mystically carved in front
findings.why_it_matters: The draft renders this as a quote fragment ('the great Heidelburgh Tun of the Sperm Whale') rather than in the declarative voice; 'great tierce' is dropped in favour of 'famous tierce,' slightly flattening the register.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the source phrasing 'famous great tierce' rather than 'famous tierce' to preserve the doubled-adjective emphasis.

findings.source_passage: though from unavoidable circumstances, considerable of it is spilled, leaks, and dribbles away, or is otherwise irrevocably lost
findings.source_locator: Paragraph beginning 'The lower subdivided part,' final sentence
findings.why_it_matters: The tricolon 'spilled, leaks, and dribbles away, or is otherwise irrevocably lost' is rhythmically distinctive; the draft reduces it to 'much is spilled and lost,' erasing the comic accumulative voice.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the original tricolon: 'spilled, leaks, and dribbles away, or is otherwise irrevocably lost in the ticklish business of securing what you can.'

summary: The draft is largely faithful and preserves most signature passages, including the pelisse simile, the closing invocation, and the Heidelburgh Tun comparisons, but drops the full quoin footnote definition (the chapter's key piece of mock-pedantic voice) and mildly flattens two other rhythmic moments.
